title: Design off-host backup so a store can honestly report local_backed_up
outcome: Design off-host backup so a store can honestly report local_backed_up
acceptance: docs/features/ holds a design brief for off-host backup that names what each copy contains and excludes, where it goes and how that target is configured, what triggers a copy, how freshness is recorded, and exactly when doctor reports local_backed_up instead of local
the brief names the restore path from an off-host copy onto a clean home and the acceptance test that proves a restored store equals the source at the copy's cut
the brief states what happens when a copy fails or goes stale, and how the operator sees it, with no silent degradation
the implementation is decomposed into Engram items, each with criteria an independent evaluator can check from the repository and command output
both architects record their concurrence on the final brief, and the questions that need Greg's decision are listed on this item

completion.summary: Off-host backup is designed and its brief is on master. docs/features/off-host-backup.md names two copy kinds (the verified full-store file and the unwidened work-graph document), the BackupAdapter port with the directory and git-ref adapters, target configuration with the operator's disclosure authorization and off-host assertion, the eight-step push with its lock and pending-attempt record, the host trigger, the freshness rule under which doctor reports local_backed_up and the reasons it reports otherwise, the status, doctor and next surfaces, restore from either kind onto a clean home with the store-equality acceptance test, and the acceptance tests. Nine companion documents were aligned with it. Implementation is filed as root w-5627a19713d8 with eight required children and the later root w-121c35181dea. Both architects concurred on the landed text and the coordinator approved it; three landing-review rounds by Engram::Opus found and I fixed every Medium, and the one remaining Low is filed as w-1b24f538375a. Landed by Engram::Opus as a Markdown-only changeset; nothing was built or installed. The independent acceptance evaluation 01a8f7af44394b4382c29658695cf7c2 passed all five criteria.
